input.content: Pattern: enforcing a new protocol field unconditionally breaks backward compatibility with an independently-released counterpart. In save_settings (enhanced-settings task 1), the client began requiring response["applied"] is True and sending require_receipt:True on EVERY save, but the supported provider at git tag eval-release returns only {"ok": True}. Because the receipt behavior was not gated behind the existing enhanced_settings flag (default False), ordinary saves against the supported provider always raise RuntimeError, violating the stated requirement that ordinary saves keep working while enhanced_settings is false. Review signal: when a client and provider release independently and a feature flag exists, new protocol requirements (new required response fields, new request flags) MUST be gated behind that flag; verify against the actual released counterpart source, not against a test stub. Secondary signal: the unit test was updated to return the new field (applied:True), which masks the regression because the stub no longer matches the real provider contract — assert new negative/raise paths and keep stubs faithful to the released contract.
